description: The repository shall maintain this catalog as the canonical record of Constellation requirements, ownership, implementation evidence, verification, milestones, release scope, sources, and known limitations.
notes: The schema preserves the common Taskyon and Syncpeer columns and adds Taskyon compatibility, milestone, and target-release tracking.

description: A requirement shall not be marked tracked or implemented until its owning implementation path and focused verification evidence are recorded.
notes: Existing Taskyon or Syncpeer behavior is dependency evidence, not Constellation implementation evidence.

description: Every requirement shall classify its relationship to Taskyon as native protocol reuse, layered application behavior, a runtime adapter, or local Constellation behavior.
notes: Allowed values are native, layered, adapter, and local.

description: Requirements shall use foundation, web-preview, v1, post-v1, or future milestones to express implementation order independently from release scope.
notes: A v1 requirement may have a foundation or web-preview milestone because target_release defines product inclusion.

description: Every requirement shall use target_release v1, post-v1, or future so the complete v1 dependency closure is directly filterable without duplicating the catalog.
notes: Milestone orders implementation; target_release defines product scope.

description: V1 shall let two real people use independently generated links to share live locations in either direction through a hosted browser app or Android app, observe freshness and viewers, and stop or revoke access without developer tooling.
notes: Reciprocity in v1 uses two independent one-way links; mutual QR pairing is deferred.

description: Constellation shall be distributed under the MIT License with copyright held by Xyntopia.
verification: LICENSE contains the standard MIT License text and Copyright (c) 2026 Xyntopia.
notes: The license applies to the Constellation repository; reused dependencies retain their own licenses.

description: Constellation shall consume versioned narrow Taskyon packages for FRP streams, P2P, Space capabilities, sensor protocols, and maps rather than importing sibling source paths or copying implementations.
notes: Taskyon packages are currently private workspaces and require an upstream supported distribution boundary.

description: Constellation shall use pinned Taskyon-owned TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, and Vite configuration through a supported shared package.
notes: Configuration shall have one upstream owner rather than copied files that drift.

description: Taskyon shall expose its MapLibre, PMTiles, and range-cache behavior through a narrow reusable package that does not require the complete Taskyon UI dependency graph.
notes: Constellation shall not vendor the existing map implementation.

description: Constellation shall supersede the unauthenticated in-memory Deno and SSE location prototype after equivalent basic live sharing is verified.
notes: The prototype remains a UX reference and is not a production compatibility contract.

description: Taskyon shall define a transport-independent read-only sensor service for dynamically described sensors and signed observations.
notes: V1 implements and advertises only the standard location profile while preserving the generic endpoint, grant, and stream contract.

description: A peer shall declare zero or more stable sensor endpoints without requiring a centrally fixed list of sensor kinds.
notes: Declarations are descriptive and grant no authority by themselves.

description: Each sensor endpoint shall identify a versioned profile or canonical schema revision, value shape, units, quality metadata, stream behavior, and owning service principal.
notes: V1 interprets only the location profile and rejects unsupported required profiles without executing custom semantics.

description: The sensor model shall support interoperable Taskyon standard profiles and dynamically declared custom schemas through the same descriptor mechanism.
notes: Profile interpretation remains separate from transport and discovery.

description: Every observation shall bind its sensor identifier, descriptor revision, source principal, monotonic sequence, capture time, value payload, and quality metadata to an authenticated source envelope.
notes: Receivers reject invalid signatures, schemas, bounds, and replayed or regressing sequences.

description: Authorized consumers shall receive current and subsequent observations through one bounded FRP stream with cancellation and backpressure.
notes: The first valid event supplies current state so a duplicate current-value command is unnecessary.

description: A separately authorized sensor-history capability shall stream a bounded time range without exposing provider paths or an unbounded query surface.
notes: Constellation initially permits at most the latest 30 minutes for remote location views.

description: A signed expiring service advertisement shall identify protocol and descriptor revisions, routing information, limits, and expiry without revealing private Space membership.
notes: Advertisement proves neither authorization nor correct behavior.

description: Space or transient-share grants shall independently authorize publish-own and read-current operations for explicit sensors and bounded scopes.
notes: Read access never implies publication, history access, delegation, device control, or Space administration.

description: Writable attributes and device commands shall remain outside the first sensor protocol and require a separate future command capability and authorization review.
notes: A generic sensor declaration must not become an unrestricted remote-control surface.

description: Sensor endpoint, profile, attribute, and event concepts shall preserve a clean future mapping to Matter while making no initial Matter wire-compatibility claim.
source: Connectivity Standards Alliance Matter specification;Thread Group resources
notes: A Matter bridge will be a separately authorized and tested adapter.

description: Constellation shall treat libp2p as connectivity fabric and the Taskyon sensor protocol as the application layer rather than coupling sensor semantics to one network transport.
notes: This is architectural alignment, not Thread protocol implementation.

description: Taskyon shall define a versioned location profile carrying latitude, longitude, capture time, accuracy, and optional altitude, heading, and speed.
notes: The profile shall define numeric bounds, units, optional-field semantics, and freshness behavior.

description: Location observations shall use source-owned monotonic sequences and explicit capture and expiry times so receivers can reject replay and display stale state honestly.
notes: Wall-clock timestamps alone shall not decide ordering or authorization.

description: A publishing device shall adapt sampling to movement, elapsed time, requested detail, power state, and a maximum interval through simple battery-versus-detail presets.
notes: Continuous maximum-rate GPS is not the default.

description: The source shall choose exact or approximate disclosure independently for each active share and shall always see the active choice.
notes: New shares default to approximate; choosing exact is explicit, and the raw exact sample remains local when approximate sharing is selected.

description: Approximate sharing shall transform coordinates on the source with a keyed offset that is shared by all approximate recipients and rotates on a multi-hour epoch rather than changing per sample or per receiver.
notes: The initial target is a neighborhood-scale area of roughly one kilometre; the rotation interval requires focused privacy testing before it becomes a fixed default.

description: The UI and documentation shall state that long movement patterns or collusion with a recipient who has exact access can still reveal sensitive location information.
notes: Approximation reduces precision; it does not provide anonymity.

description: A viewer shall distinguish live, delayed, stale, expired, revoked, and unavailable location state instead of silently presenting old coordinates as current.
notes: Age and source expiry remain visible on the map and member surface.

description: Constellation shall present one local person identity with independently named and revocable device identities, each of which may publish its own authorized location.
notes: A device identity does not independently grant broad access to user or Space data.

description: A new source or viewer shall receive a local device identity without registration, hosted account authentication, or disclosure of a stable identity to other link recipients.
notes: Deleting local application data may destroy the local identity and active shares; account recovery is outside v1.

description: Background publishers shall receive a narrow device-bound principal and publish-own grant without receiving Space administration or read access to unrelated sensors.
notes: This is the unattended-service boundary used while the phone is locked.

description: Missing membership, grant, publication, or distribution policy shall deny location access.
notes: Global discovery never advertises Space membership.

description: The initial UI shall expose shares and connections rather than requiring users to understand Space keys, overlays, grants, or service advertisements.
notes: Security mechanics remain inspectable in diagnostics and advanced details.

description: A future named family or friends group shall be an independent collaborative Space rather than an extension of the user's default personal Space.
notes: Location publication remains opt-in per Space.

description: Ordinary group members shall be able to publish their own location and view members who currently choose to share, while administrators alone manage membership.
notes: Joining a group never starts location sharing automatically.

description: Named collaborative Spaces shall support promotion and revocation of multiple administrators and explicit ownership transfer.
notes: Administration remains separate from ordinary membership and device control.

description: Named collaborative Spaces shall support an offline recovery secret without putting root keys or reusable administrator credentials in invitations, links, logs, or QR codes.
notes: Recovery requires bootstrap access to an authorized provider or rendezvous network.

description: Equivalent location data shared into different transient share scopes shall be encrypted independently to reduce provider-side correlation.
notes: Each live share projection is derived from the current source observation and encrypted for only its authorized scope; named Spaces inherit this rule post-v1.

description: Persistent Space enrollment shall use short-lived single-use QR or invite links with out-of-band fingerprint confirmation and existing-administrator approval.
notes: This enrollment flow is distinct from pre-authorized transient location links.

description: A location link shall create a narrow encrypted share scope and read grant without enrolling receivers as people, devices, or members of a collaborative Space.
notes: Receivers gain no history ownership, delegation, publication, device-control, or administration authority.

description: The share URL shall place the bearer capability in its fragment and shall not expose it to HTTP requests, referrers, logs, analytics, or messenger link-preview fetches.
notes: The landing page performs no redemption until the receiver explicitly accepts.

description: The web and Android apps shall use the system share surface so a source can send the generated URL through Signal or another installed messenger without messenger-specific account integration.
notes: The security contract belongs to the link, not the messenger.

description: A source shall choose duration, precision, and viewer capacity before generating a link so valid receivers need no later source approval.
notes: V1 links grant current location only; the source may revoke the whole link or individual active sessions at any time.

description: A multi-recipient link shall expose only the source's authorized location; receivers shall not discover one another or gain reciprocal sharing automatically.
notes: Two people share in both directions in v1 by independently creating and sending one-way links; mutual QR pairing is post-v1.

description: Sharing shall default to one hour, offer longer presets including eight hours, and stop publication and retrieval automatically at expiry.
notes: Sharing is off by default.

description: An until-revoked link shall exist only as an advanced option behind a prominent warning and explicit source confirmation.
notes: Until-revoked is never the default and remains manually revocable.

description: A source shall select a viewer capacity with quick choices of one, ten, and fifty plus an advanced no-share-level-cap option.
notes: No share-level cap is still subject to relay quotas, rate limits, and abuse controls and is not an infinite-capacity promise.

description: Each successful link redemption shall create a separate ephemeral viewer session so forwarding and concurrent use can be counted, bounded, and revoked.
notes: A session is not a persistent person identity.

description: Viewer sessions shall send bounded heartbeats so the source can see active receiver count, optional receiver-provided labels, ephemeral fingerprints, and last-seen freshness.
notes: Presence may be delayed or unknown while the source is disconnected.

description: The source shall be able to revoke one viewer session without revoking every receiver using the same link.
notes: Revocation prevents future access but cannot erase already observed information.

description: The product shall describe active viewers as connected Constellation sessions and shall not claim to count screenshots, copied coordinates, modified clients, or downstream rebroadcasts.
notes: Viewer counts are operational presence, not proof of human attention or non-retention.

description: Two devices shall establish reciprocal view grants through a hidden pair scope after both people independently confirm their own duration and precision.
notes: Stopping or expiring one direction does not silently stop or extend the other direction.

description: The map screen and Android notification shall continuously show whether sharing is active, its recipients or scope, precision, expiry, and a one-action stop control.
notes: Background collection must never be visually silent.

description: V1 clients and providers shall not persist exact or approximate location observations; an already connected viewer may retain only its current point in memory until the view closes or the share becomes unavailable.
notes: A new viewer waits for the source when it is offline; durable self-history and provider-hosted last-known state are post-v1.

description: Remote trail access shall expose only bounded viewing streams with no export operation or persistent viewer cache while acknowledging that an authorized viewer can capture rendered data.
notes: The protocol shall not make an unenforceable DRM claim.

description: A device's durable trail shall contain only samples generated by that device and shall never append locations received from another peer.
notes: This prevents ordinary viewers from becoming accidental history replicas or onward publishers.

description: A device shall append self-generated samples to bounded daily text journals containing a versioned header and one authenticated base64url ciphertext envelope per line.
notes: No database is required; plaintext coordinates never enter the journal.

description: Journal envelopes shall authenticate device identity, format version, sequence, capture time, and previous-envelope commitment so truncation, reordering, replay, and corruption are detected.
notes: Recovery may preserve valid prefixes while reporting damaged or missing suffixes.

description: Completed daily or size-bounded journals shall rotate into signed immutable segments suitable for verification and optional blind replication.
notes: Mutable current journals remain local and have one owning writer.

description: Self-history shall default to thirty days and offer shorter periods or keep-until-deleted; cleanup shall remove complete expired segments and their keys or envelopes.
notes: Retention changes do not silently publish or replicate history.

description: Android shall protect the local trail key with Android Keystore so an explicitly started background share can continue after screen lock without exposing a broad Space or user root key.
notes: Behavior after reboot follows platform protected-data availability and fails closed when the key is unavailable.

description: A source shall derive the minimum authorized time range from local self-history and encrypt a separate projection for each Space or transient share scope.
notes: Canonical self-history is never handed directly to a remote provider.

description: Selected storage services may retain opaque source-authored immutable trail segments without receiving plaintext, Space membership, or decryption authority.
notes: Ordinary viewer devices do not satisfy replica durability targets.

description: A source may grant remote viewers access to at most the latest thirty minutes of its trail through a bounded memory-only stream.
notes: The viewer discards the window on close, expiry, or revocation.

description: Official clients shall not write another device's received trail to persistent storage or re-advertise it as a local sensor history.
notes: A malicious authorized client can still capture plaintext and is outside this enforceable guarantee.

description: The web app shall use Taskyon browser libp2p with WebRTC, WebTransport, secure WebSockets, and circuit-relay transport as available.
notes: Runtime capability detection shall report unavailable transports without weakening authorization.

description: Taskyon P2P shall provide a js-libp2p transport adapter backed by Tauri native sockets so Android is not limited to browser WebRTC connectivity.
notes: The adapter belongs upstream in Taskyon and must preserve the same peer identity and stream semantics.

feature: Native HTTP and secure relay access
description: The Android host shall expose bounded native HTTP or secure WebSocket connectivity needed for bootstrap, relay, and provider access without exposing generic unrestricted network calls to the UI.
notes: Native networking is capability-scoped and uses the same service contracts as web transports.

description: Peers shall try compatible direct transports first and then configured Taskyon circuit relays and gateways with bounded retries and backoff.
notes: Transport choice never changes location protocol semantics; user-configurable self-hosted providers are post-v1.

description: V1 shall operate production bootstrap, rendezvous, secure WebSocket or WebTransport, and circuit-relay endpoints separately from the static web app so browser and Android peers can connect when direct paths fail.
notes: The service deployment is Taskyon-operated, transports only authorization-scoped encrypted traffic, and cannot guarantee networks that block every outbound path.

description: A Space or advanced user shall be able to configure additional bootstrap, relay, and blind-storage providers without replacing the Taskyon protocol.
notes: Provider selection remains separate from service advertisement and authorization.

description: Share and Space traffic shall use cryptographically separate overlays whose identifiers, grants, and contents are absent from global discovery.
notes: Several overlays may multiplex one authenticated peer connection.

description: Relays shall forward opaque encrypted traffic without receiving location plaintext, reusable share capabilities, or collaborative Space membership.
notes: A member relay is a distinct explicitly granted service principal.

description: An authorized blind provider may retain the newest encrypted location observation and its expiry so receivers can distinguish last-known state while the source is temporarily unreachable.
notes: Expired state is unavailable and is removed according to provider policy.

description: The product shall not promise connectivity through total network loss, captive portals, or networks that block every available outbound transport.
notes: Diagnostics identify direct, relayed, offline, blocked, and degraded states.

description: Relays and publishers shall enforce bounded messages, stream counts, heartbeats, quotas, rates, and expiries before allocating unbounded work.
notes: An uncapped share still operates within infrastructure safety limits; later storage and history services define their own bounds.

description: The primary surface shall be a full-screen share map with one prominent sharing and expiry control and a compact connections drawer.
notes: Space terminology remains absent from the default workflow.

description: The initial app shall keep the map, active shares, link creation, viewer management, and diagnostics reachable without introducing a broad dashboard.
notes: QR pairing, history, provider configuration, and cryptographic details remain absent or secondary according to their target release.

description: Constellation shall render current location points, accuracy or approximate areas, and stale state through the published Taskyon MapLibre component.
notes: Location overlays are derived locally from authorized observations; trail rendering is post-v1.

description: The map shall use the configured Taskyon PMTiles archive and shall not silently contact a third-party raster-tile fallback.
notes: Failure leaves sharing operational and shows a clear cached or blank map state.

description: Every successfully requested PMTiles byte range shall be retained through the Taskyon StorageClient range cache under a bounded LRU policy.
notes: No background area or whole-world prefetch is required.

description: The app shall continue to render cached map ranges and location overlays while offline and shall visibly indicate unavailable uncached basemap data.
notes: Location exchange and collection do not depend on map-tile availability.

description: The web application shall use Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript, Vue Router, and small local UI components without importing the full Quasar application stack.
notes: The same frontend is embedded by Tauri.

description: Modern mobile and desktop browsers shall create and view shares while the page remains active, and shall clearly report that publication may stop when the browser suspends or closes the page.
notes: Reliable screen-locked background publication requires the Android app; installable PWA behavior is post-v1.

description: The production Vue application shall be deployed as a static site at https://constellation.taskyon.space with SPA routing and share fragments preserved entirely on the client.
notes: The build shall be compatible with a Pages host; changing the static hosting provider does not change the share protocol.

description: The web build shall be installable as a secure-context PWA while stating that browser background location is not reliable after suspension.
notes: Foreground browser sharing is the supported web guarantee.

description: The Android application shall package the shared Vue frontend with Tauri 2 and keep Android-only location, key, socket, notification, and background-service behavior behind native adapters.
notes: V1 targets SDK 36 and supports Android 10/API 29 and newer; shared core modules do not import Android APIs.

description: Explicitly started Android sharing shall continue collection and publication in a foreground service with a persistent status notification and stop action.
notes: The app requests only platform permissions required by the selected behavior.

description: Backgrounding shall close the Activity-owned P2P session before the foreground service starts its own protected JavaScript runtime and native-socket session; foregrounding performs the reverse handoff.
notes: Overlapping owners must not duplicate publication or contend for identity state.

description: The foreground service shall persist a bounded encrypted sharing request and recover after process recreation, network change, or Android service restart without extending its original expiry.
notes: Repeated startup failure uses bounded backoff and fails closed.

description: Background sharing shall expose understandable battery and metered-network policy while preserving the user's explicit active-share intent and expiry.
notes: Policy pauses are visible and do not masquerade as live publication.

description: The app shall explain foreground and background location permission separately, degrade safely when either is denied, and never infer consent from Space membership or a prior share.
notes: Permission prompts follow an explicit user action.

description: The repository shall provide reproducible Tauri Android development, signed release, artifact-copy, emulator, and physical-device workflows modeled on Syncpeer.
notes: A tagged forge-neutral project release publishes the signed APK and checksum; signing credentials remain outside the repository.

description: Approximation secrets, share capabilities, viewer sessions, device identities, and background sharing requests shall be authenticated and encrypted before ordinary persistent storage.
notes: V1 does not persist location observations; PMTiles are public map data and use a separate cache policy.

description: Logs, diagnostics, tests, crash reports, URLs, filenames, and CI artifacts shall exclude raw coordinates, bearer fragments, Space secrets, private peer addresses, recovery material, and real personal identifiers.
notes: Tests use synthetic coordinates, identities, and network metadata.

description: Every live location or presence request shall validate the exact grant, sensor, scope, operation, expiry, and resource limits before reading or subscribing to data.
notes: Denied requests must not read a current observation or reveal whether location data exists; later history capabilities require independent authorization.

description: The UI shall explain that revocation prevents future authorized retrieval but cannot erase coordinates already observed, copied, photographed, or retained by a recipient.
notes: No client-side control can enforce deletion after plaintext has been displayed.

description: Sensor, location, share, and transport contracts shall negotiate explicit versions and reject unsupported required semantics without silently widening access.
notes: Unknown optional sensor profiles remain opaque and non-executable.

description: Focused diagnostics shall prove two browser peers exchange authorized location observations directly when possible and through a local relay fallback.
notes: The result identifies the actual transport and never uses production identities.

description: Tests shall cover URL-fragment secrecy, preview fetches, explicit acceptance, multi-session capacity, expiry, whole-link and per-session revocation, and heartbeat presence.
notes: Synthetic links and viewers only.

description: Tests shall prove unauthorized, expired, revoked, wrong-sensor, wrong-scope, and replayed requests are denied before current location state is read or subscribed.
notes: Capability support and service advertisement alone never authorize access.

description: Tests shall prove equivalent observations produce independently encrypted messages for separate transient share scopes.
notes: Named Space coverage is added with that post-v1 feature; provider-visible metadata is reviewed for residual size and timing leakage.

description: Tests shall verify journal parsing, authentication, sequence integrity, corruption isolation, rotation, retention deletion, and absence of plaintext coordinates.
notes: Fixtures use synthetic paths, identities, keys, and coordinates.

description: Tests shall request map ranges, disconnect the source, verify cached reuse and eviction limits, and confirm that no third-party tile host is contacted.
notes: Map failure must not stop location collection or exchange.

description: Android tests shall cover foreground-service startup, notification stop, screen lock, Activity handoff, process recreation, reboot, expiry, permission denial, metered policy, power policy, and network transitions.
notes: Emulator evidence does not replace physical-phone acceptance.

description: A browser peer and Android background peer shall exchange the same versioned sensor protocol over direct and relayed paths without platform-specific location semantics.
notes: The native socket adapter requires external-consumer conformance coverage.

description: A self-contained sandbox harness shall build an x86_64 test APK, own API 29 compatibility and API 36 modern AVDs, install and drive the app through ADB and WebView automation, inject synthetic locations, and exchange locations with a host dev server and browser peer through 10.0.2.2 over direct and relayed paths.
notes: The harness uses KVM when available, requires an empty managed ADB device set, cleans up on failure, and covers restart, abrupt termination, expiry, revocation, and network transitions without recording real device data.

description: Release diagnostics shall classify direct, relayed, reconnecting, offline, captive-portal, and fully blocked scenarios across representative browser and Android networks.
notes: Failures outside available transports are reported rather than hidden or claimed as supported.

description: A signed release build shall pass background sharing, lock, reboot, process death, network handoff, battery policy, and long-running expiry scenarios on representative supported physical Android 10 and newer devices before v1 release.
notes: Emulator-only success is insufficient for background-location, vendor power-management, and radio-transition claims.
